subject: Marketplace private offer: distributor padding, ceiling adjustments and billing flow
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenWave Solutions Procurement <procure@greenwave.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on pricing ceiling and distributor offset for private offer

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks for the draft private offer you sent last week. GreenWave procurement asked us to confirm two operational items before we can move to legal: 1) how you want us to handle distributor rounding/ceiling when marketplace SKUs are listed at tiered prices, and 2) whether Redwood can absorb a small distributor offset (to keep channel economics stable) or if GreenWave needs to accept a pass-through line on their invoice.

Specific asks from GreenWave:
- A short example (math) showing list price -> marketplace final price -> distributor net after commissions and marketplace fees.
- A proposed policy for rounding when marketplace prices are bucketed (they want price floors / ceilings clarified).
- A mechanism for monthly true-up if usage is under commit (they want to avoid surprise credits).

Attached: proposal-v2.xlsx with the private offer draft.

Can you confirm operational flow (who invoices whom) and whether Redwood can provide a 1–3% distributor padding for rounding, or if we should add a pass-through line item?

Best,
Marco
CloudDist Partnerships

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing ceiling and distributor offset for private offer

Thanks Marco — received. Looping in Ben and Karthik to propose a clean waterfall and ops approach. High level we can:

- Show a sample waterfall and workback on a $100k monthly commit to illustrate rounding and discounts.
- Offer a distributor padding (small %) that sits between list price and marketplace list to protect channel margins.
- Define a monthly true-up reconciliation with a capped retro credit (e.g., 2 months lookback) to limit financial exposure.

Ben / Karthik — can you draft the waterfall + suggested padding bands (we prefer not to put a visible pass-through line on the GreenWave invoice if we can avoid it; distributor prefers it be implicit).

Soojin
Head of Channel Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com>, GreenWave Solutions Procurement <procure@greenwave.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing ceiling and distributor offset for private offer

Folks — attaching redwood-marketplace-pricing-matrix.pdf with a proposed margin waterfall and a worked example. Summary below:

Proposed waterfall (example math on $100k list):
- Marketplace listed price (public SKU): $100,000
- Marketplace fees (~3%): $3,000 (deducted by marketplace before payout)
- Distributor commission (recommended): 8% of net after marketplace fee = $7,760
- Reseller margin (if applicable): 10% of customer invoice = $10,000
- Redwood net (after fees & commissions): ~$79,240

Padding / rounding policy options:
1) Fixed padding band: Redwood reserves a 2% distributor padding to absorb rounding and fee variability.
2) Ceiling rule: If computed final price falls within a bucket, we round up to the next cent and absorb up to 1% variance; anything above triggers a manual true-up.
3) Visible pass-through: add a "marketplace fees" line on the invoice (less preferred).

Recommendation: Use Fixed padding band (2%) + monthly reconciliation. That keeps invoices clean for GreenWave and keeps the distributor economics predictable. For commitments under the target, propose a capped retro credit equal to the padding difference, reconciled monthly with a 60-day limit.

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-pricing-matrix.pdf (contains the worked example and CSV-friendly table).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Partner Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenWave Solutions Procurement <procure@greenwave.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing ceiling and distributor offset for private offer

Thanks Ben — the waterfall is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:

- GreenWave accepts the 2% fixed padding conceptally, but asks for a clear monthly true-up process if monthly usage is 20% below committed volume. They want the cap on retro credits tied to the padding (so it can't exceed the padding + 1 month).
- They also want marketplace fees to be transparent in the contract (not necessarily on the customer invoice) so their finance team can audit the math.

Operational ask: who does the primary invoice? (CloudDist can pass through the marketplace invoice, Redwood can also invoice the reseller and issue a credit — we need a flow diagram). Can you propose a preferred flow that minimizes reconciliation friction?

Marco

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenWave Solutions Procurement <procure@greenwave.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing ceiling and distributor offset for private offer

On Tue, Apr 22, 2027 at 11:20 AM Marco Rossi <marco@clouddist.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — the waterfall is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement: ...

Hi all — proposed operational flow below (keeps GreenWave invoicing simple and limits party-to-party reconciliation):

Operational billing flow (preferred):
1) GreenWave is billed by CloudDist via the marketplace listing (marketplace issues invoice to GreenWave as standard).
2) Marketplace remits payout to CloudDist net of marketplace fees.
3) CloudDist issues a statement of earned commissions to Redwood for reconciliation.
4) Redwood issues a monthly rebate/credit to CloudDist (or directly to GreenWave if requested) to honor the private offer discount; this credit is capped by the agreed padding + 1 month true-up.

Key guardrails:
- Monthly true-up window: 30 days to surface usage variances; 60 days to effect credits.
- Retro cap: no more than padding + 1 month of difference (example: padding 2% => cap 3% retro).
- Rounding hedge: add a 0.5% operational buffer on top of the 2% distributor padding for marketplaces with coarse bucketing.

Next steps:
- We'll prepare a one-page ops runbook and a reconciliations template.
- Legal / procurement: if GreenWave wants marketplace fees logged in the contract, we can include a quoted appendix with the waterfall math (not a separate invoice line).

Attaching: pricing-matrix-final.xlsx (finalized with reconciliation cadence and example numbers).

—Karthik
Director, Cloud Marketplace Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is actionable. Quick summary and next steps: 

Summary decisions:
- We will adopt the Fixed padding band model: 2% distributor padding + 0.5% rounding hedge.
- Monthly true-up with a cap (padding + 1 month) and a 60-day credit effect window.
- Marketplace fees will be documented in an appendix for auditability (not a visible customer invoice line).

Action items:
